A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Mixed Signals dataset and retain matching core benchmarks and figures. Their complete texts and appendices are readable, including v2's added labeling specification, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset analyses, annotation-quality visualizations, and detection and communication-bandwidth results in Tables 3–4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds cross-dataset transfer evaluations and preliminary tracking results in Appendix Table A2.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the dataset construction pipeline and PointPillar-based OpenCOOD adaptations with additional 1-by-1 convolutional detection heads. v2 evaluates existing methods in additional settings and documents annotation procedures; it does not establish a revision to the proposed algorithms or architectures.

E1.justification: Coverage expands beyond the two detection benchmarks to evaluated multi-object tracking and transfer from V2V4Real-trained models to Mixed Signals. Tracking introduces temporal identity requirements, while transfer tests a different training domain. The collected dataset, categories, and original detection tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v2 adds AB3DMOT as an evaluated tracking baseline in Appendix B.2/Table A2. The original detection comparator set remains intact; the additional Early/Late Fusion rows represent existing methods under different training conditions.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation of V2V4Real-trained detectors and tracking using V2X-ViT detections with sAMOTA, AMOTA, and AMOTP. The tracking table names a validation split without defining its composition. Existing detection splits, visibility thresholds, evaluation region, AP metrics, and bandwidth measurement remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.3.1 adds a domain-transfer analysis using Early and Late Fusion, accompanied by heading-error examples in the new Figure 11. Existing alignment, annotation-consistency, intensity, and distribution analyses are retained; moving the intensity analysis to the appendix does not constitute a new analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report individual benchmark scores and descriptive dataset statistics without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added experiments introduce no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: All original scores in Tables 3–4 remain unchanged. Table 3 adds V2V4Real-trained Early/Late Fusion vehicle AP of 0.24/0.12 at both reported IoU thresholds. Table A2 adds tracking sAMOTA/AMOTA/AMOTP of 89.6/43.1/63.3 for vehicles and 76.6/32.6/42.8 for pedestrians. These are additional settings and task outcomes, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: No formal definitions, assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised. Existing task definitions and synchronization reasoning are retained. The newly reported tracking metrics are named without introducing mathematical development.

C1.justification: v2 narrows the novelty claim from heterogeneous CAV LiDAR setups generally to configurations differing in both position and orientation. It corrects the abstract's description of two sensor types to two configurations and replaces broad highest-quality claims with more specific alignment and annotation claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets transfer failures and incorrect headings as evidence of learned right-hand-traffic priors and sensor-related domain gaps. It also adds that uniformly using intensity values across heterogeneous agents would be inadequate. Existing fusion-bandwidth and vehicle-sensor interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v2 embeds the labeling specification previously referenced externally, documenting box geometry, extremities, occlusion, track-ID reuse, motion attributes, and labeling-tool instructions. It also identifies a separate devkit and supplies a direct repository link. These substantially expand documentation rather than establish changed procedures; the specification's 20-second/2-Hz description is not reconciled with the main text's 30-second scenes and 1-Hz annotation.

R1.justification: Table 1 now acknowledges height heterogeneity in V2V4Real and V2X-Real and distinguishes Mixed Signals by height and tilt. It also replaces the claim that marked datasets are inaccessible everywhere with geographically restricted access. v2 adds the AB3DMOT reference and a transfer-based comparison with V2V4Real, while retaining the broader related-work coverage.

P1.justification: The main section framework remains, with targeted abstract/introduction rewrites, task-specific results subsections, and expanded appendix organization. Intensity analysis, category explanations, annotation priorities, and portions of synchronization/localization discussion move into the appendix. Much of the original prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands visual documentation through the transfer-error Figure 11, tracking Table A2, and an illustrated labeling specification containing rule tables and screenshots. Table 3 gains gray transfer-result rows. The original figures remain visually unchanged, including v1 Figure 6 relocated to Appendix Figure A2.

improvement.justification: v2 improves claim precision, makes annotation practices inspectable, and adds useful transfer and preliminary tracking evidence while preserving the original benchmarks. These gains are limited by incomplete new protocols and unreconciled annotation timing. Table 3 also retains an overbroad claim that all fusion methods beat No Fusion, despite the added adapted Late Fusion score of 0.12 versus 0.17. Overall, the added transparency and more accurate positioning provide a modest net improvement.
